visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. The KB-era index.html that used to sit in this directory was DELETED 2026-08-27: it was retired as a visual target on 2026-08-26 and kept only because ci:mockup-coverage required a parity.json beside any index.html, which is a gate keeping a dead file alive. The target is the patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. competitiveTarget: Beat generic brokerage team pages AND Cascade Sotheby's Bend agent directory: real broker names, Oregon licenses, transparent-PNG headshots, and — the thing a directory does not have — each broker's OWN MLS record as a figure with the places behind a disclosure, plus a map of every closing the three of them hold.

beats.text: P6: every roster card shows the Oregon license number as a credential, not a buried footnote.
P0: the desktop hero carries the license line plus Call, Text, Email, and Schedule CTAs in the first viewport.
P3: a listings or closings rail (atlas or recorded sales) is a real second section, not a one-screen directory.
P2: Schedule stays on the reach row with Call/Text/Email — regression, never an orphaned fourth action.
Index is roster only: doors to /team/[slug]. Not a second About — no Proof, FAQ, or seller ask on /team.
Each card is a person (photo, name, title, license) not four equal hairline contact cells.
Broker profile fold: license + Call/Text/Email/Schedule. Firm proof is the default; personal record only when real.
Call is the primary conversion on cards and the profile. Text, Email, and Schedule remain. Do not invent a personal volume hero.

Still not a second About: no Proof, no FAQ, no seller ask. Per-broker figure still from getBrokerSales via broker-roster-record.ts.

tasteReview.beats: Compass agent roster (compass.com) — this page wins on sourced MLS 12-month closing counts, Oregon licenses, and an honest split between those trailing-window face figures and the map full-record closings; it loses on a specialty line and on marks you can actually read.

defects.finding: The atlas takes half the 1440 fold and claims 25 closings, but the field is empty cream with Terrebonne and Redmond labels and marks too faint to read as a record. house-atlas is already on the page and lost: this is a cream map box, not the demo hoverable data-encoded cells.

Where those closings were renders as a native select/details, not house-proof sourced-record interaction and not a drawing of the places. The live control and the catalog demo are not the same interaction.
Matt 7 closings in the last 12 months is a static digit plus a label, a figure row with no sparkline, scrub, or encoded places, so the 12-month claim has no motion that is the data.
Rebecca 3 in Bend is a number and a place with no sentence matching Matt 12-month closing claim, so the companion figure reads as a KPI chip and the two faces do not make the same kind of record.
Call is a navy chip with a phone number, not display-scale doors with live hours. Text Email Schedule are extra exits, and Schedule drops onto its own row under Rebecca.
At 375 the coverage atlas is gone. The visitor gets a three-sentence claim and one broker card, so the page differentiator is not in the first viewport.
Schedule sits on its own line under Rebecca Call button, an orphaned fourth action at 1440.

tasteReview.rebaselineReason: evaluatorModel claude-sonnet-5 to grok-4.6; rubricVersion v1-2026-09-08 to v1-2026-09-10; shotsHash changed with SITE-74 editorial capture. Table instrument to beat was 39. Honesty 8 holds.
tasteReview.verdict: Better than a 39: faces open at display scale, Call is the one primary, sourced 12-month counts sit on the faces, and a navy-on-cream Atlas is in the 1440 fold with copy that does not equate those counts with the map full-record closings. The Atlas is still faint geography; 375 does not carry the map.
